sentenceSets.sentence: The nettlesome detail that no one could resolve had been placed in a footnote, where it remained unaddressed.

answerChoices.reasoning: Intractable stresses only that a thing cannot be solved, but the sentence also shows the detail being pushed into a footnote and left there, which is how people treat something that keeps bothering them.
A trivial point would give no one any trouble, yet this one could not be resolved and had to be tucked out of sight.
Obscurity means being little known or hard to understand, whereas this detail was well enough understood for everyone to see it could not be settled.
A contentious point provokes argument between parties who take opposing sides, but the sentence describes a difficulty that no one could resolve and that was quietly shelved rather than fought over.
An erroneous detail would simply be corrected, not relegated to a footnote as an unsolved problem.
A redundant detail repeats what is already stated and would be cut rather than preserved in a footnote.
Peripheral describes where a matter sits in relation to the main argument, and the footnote already establishes its placement without explaining why no one could resolve it.
A technical detail requires specialist knowledge but can be resolved by a specialist, while this one defeated everyone.
Innocuous means harmless and untroubling, contradicting a detail that bothered everyone and got buried.
A settled matter is one already resolved, which the sentence explicitly denies.
Fragrance describes smell and cannot characterize an unresolved point in a document.

sentenceSets.sentence: For a fortnight a nettlesome cough kept waking him at three in the morning, though the doctor could find nothing wrong.

answerChoices.reasoning: Chronic means long-lasting, and a fortnight is short, while the sentence's emphasis falls on the nightly waking rather than on duration.
A debilitating complaint would leave him unable to function, but the doctor could find nothing wrong and the trouble is confined to broken sleep.
Acute describes a condition that comes on sharply and severely, whereas this one is mild enough to escape diagnosis and simply persists in disturbing him.
Contagiousness concerns whether others might catch it, a question the sentence never raises, since the trouble described is entirely his own broken nights.
A productive cough is one that brings up phlegm, a clinical distinction that would have given the doctor something to find.
Every cough is audible, so the word would say nothing about why this one mattered for a fortnight.
Hereditary conditions are inherited, and nothing in the sentence concerns his family or his history.
Seasonal ailments recur with the time of year, but the sentence follows a single fortnight and its three o'clock wakings.
A soothing cough is a contradiction, and nothing that woke him nightly could be described as calming.
An imaginary cough would not wake him at a particular hour for fourteen nights running.
Melodious describes pleasing music and cannot apply to something that ruined his sleep.

sentenceSets.sentence: Her habit of repeating the last three words of every sentence he spoke was nettlesome in a way he found impossible to complain about without sounding petty.

answerChoices.reasoning: Grating describes a harshness that assaults the senses, but a quiet verbal habit works by small persistent needling rather than by abrasive noise.
Something offensive gives real affront and would justify a complaint, whereas the sentence turns on his inability to object without seeming small-minded.
Insufferable means past all bearing, which cannot be true of a habit he continues to endure precisely because objecting would look petty.
An endearing habit inspires affection, the opposite of one he privately wishes he could raise as a grievance.
Deliberate concerns whether she meant to do it, a question of intent that the sentence leaves open while describing the effect on him.
Eccentricity is mere oddity, which would puzzle rather than irritate him into wanting to complain.
Unconscious describes her awareness of the habit, not the effect that makes him want to raise it and stops him.
Audibility is a bare fact about speech and says nothing about why the repetition troubled him.
A soothing habit would calm him, contradicting the urge to complain that he keeps suppressing.
The habit consists of repeating his words aloud, so it cannot be silent.
Profitability concerns financial gain and has no bearing on a conversational mannerism.
